To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intra-site variability of the dental traits analyzed here can be used to estimate population dynamics, and that it is higher among the most important sites in terms of social, political and/or economic status.

(1) the highest intra-population variability in dental morphological traits is reached when the frequency of presence of a trait and its absence are equal to 50% each; and (2), the highest values of intra-population dental variability are observed among Prehispanic Maya populations that are more integrated into regional socio-political and economic spheres of influence, and among those with higher population density.

(a) intra-population dental variability is higher when populations are in contact and gene flow is intense, and lower when populations are more isolated or kin-related; and (b) the higher intra-population variability of the Maya populations from Yucatán correlates with their position within the region's sphere of influence. © 2012 Elsevier B.V.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of intra-population variability in dental morphological traits and with the interpretation of these values within a socio-political context.

the estimation of intra-population dental variability as a proxy for the intensity of population dynamics and gene-flow, and the use of this proxy to understand the social and political organization of the Prehispanic Yucatán Maya.
the use of dental morphological variability as an indicator of social and economic dynamics in Prehispanic Maya communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, when a population is exposed to intense social, political or economic interaction with other groups, its internal variability is expected to be high.
the higher the internal variability is, the more intense the social, political and/or economic interaction of the community is with the outside world.

the more isolated the site, the lower the internal variability of dental morphology; and the higher the internal variability of a site, the more intense its participation in the regional socio-political and economic sphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is a useful and simple way to estimate intra-population dental morphologic variability.
the more isolated and kin-related groups show less internal variability, and the more integrated and complex groups show higher variability.

the more isolated a population, the lower is the intra-site variability of its dental morphological features, while the higher the population density and the greater the social, political and economical interactions among sites, the greater is the variability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the approach proposed is useful to identify the most variable samples within a population, and therefore, the ones most likely to be influenced by intense gene flow and population dynamics.

intra-population variability can be estimated from the frequency of presence of a given trait in the population and that it is possible to rank the degree of internal variability among different populations.
the proposed approach is useful in assessing the degree of internal variability in a population, which in turn may reflect the level of interaction with other groups.
